newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks soar to record close on Telmex.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks soar to record close on Telmex.

text.p: Mexican stocks took their cue from market heavyweight Telmex to rally to a record close Monday.
The blue chip IPC index closed up 95.22 points, or 2.80 percent, at 3,492.17.
Telmex L series shares, which weigh most heavily in calculating the IPC, ended up 0.98 centavos (12 cents) at 14.00 pesos ($1.78).
For some traders Monday was the first real session of the year after the holiday season. Trading volume was normal at 72.9 million shares but improved on many recent sessions.
"The year really did start on the bourse today. We feel that buyers responded to gains by Telmex and on Wall Street," said Daniel Romo of the Bancrecer bank.

Dealers noted that CS Boston upgraded Telmex stock to a buy from hold during the session, while Bear Stearns raised its 1997 and 1998 earnings estimates. Both brokerages said hikes in local call charges as of Jan. 1 were a factor.
Telmex ADRs also climbed 2-1/2 to 35-7/8 in New York.
"It was high time dealers took a good look at Telmex. It was in heavy demand from foreign investors," a trader said.
Analysts noted that blue chip stocks other than Telmex also gained on a combination of expected forthcoming falls in primary rates and technical factors.
Analysts noted that after breaking the previous record close of 3,433.75 -- set Aug. 27 -- the IPC was now in a band ranging between 3,454 and 3,530 points.
"Nonetheless, we first need to validate the 3,500-point mark with a bit more volume," the analyst added.
Money market traders said they expected primary rates on bellwether 28-day Cetes, or Treasury bills, to fall by up to three-quarters of a percentage point at Tuesday's primary auction.

Blue chips that chalked up notable gains included media group Televisa and holding company Alfa, up 2.50 (32 cents) and 1.40 pesos (18 cents), respectively, to 103.30 pesos ($13.16) and 37.90 pesos ($4.83).
The broad market scoreboard reflected the optimistic mood for blue chips. Out of a total of 103 stocks traded, gainers trounced decliners by 71 to 20.
Pharamceutical firm Autrey headed the gainers, up 1.40 pesos (18 cents) to 16.50 pesos. "Autrey had lagged behind the market and had to wait until today to get moving," a floor trader said.
Hotel operator Posadas headed the decliners, off 16 centavos (2 cents) at 3.40 pesos (43 cents).
"Most falls were speculative or on profit-taking, nothing special. Most dealers were too optimistic to sell very much," a trader said.
